messages.subject: Software Output Check
parts:
Good afternoon!

 

I am looking for feedback on this output I got using the windows distance sampling software.

 

I am analyzing multiple surveys that took course over the course of two years. In total there are around ~20 surveys with multiple entries for each survey. 

 

I set the settings so that they would average the values of all sightings over the course of the study, rather than separating them by year, month, etc.

 

The detection function looks good, but the numbers seem a little bit low. I can’t see any errors from the software perspective. I just wanted to make sure that there aren’t any aspects that I am missing since I’m not too familiar with the software.

 

Looking forward to hearing from you.


Best,

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Software Output Check
parts:
Michael

Welcome to the list. Before we can deduce whether the software is doing the "right thing", we need to understand the design of your study. There is not enough information in your screen shots to  make your design obvious. In one screenshot you have an Area associated with your Regions, in other shots you do not.

Simply describe your study area, I believe you are calling it Peafowl District 13; what is its size? Include its area as a field in the Study Area layer.

How many transects did you walk when sampling your study area; your Word document output states there were 35 transects; is that accurate? One of your screenshots suggests each of the 35 transects are 896.6m in length. That sends up a flag for me; I would be surprised if spatially replicated transects are all the same length.

It seems more likely to me that you have a small number of transects (perhaps only a single transect) that you visited many times (28Jun2020, 12Jul2020, ...).

The effort of 88803.4 (Word document) doesn't seem to correspond to one of your screen shots (35 transects each of length 896.6, which would lead to effort of 31381m.

Once we get these details sorted, then we can ensure the data are correctly entered and the analysis can begin.

Meanwhile, have a look at some of the sample projects that come with the Distance for Windows software for ideas about data organisation. Have a read through the Users Guide, specifically Chapter 5 on data structures.
